$comment: Conformance corpus shared by the web player and the iOS app. Every case is a whole tutorial document; the manifest says what each player must decide about it. 'expect' is the shared verdict. A 'web' or 'ios' block adds assertions for that player, and an 'expect' inside one of those blocks records a DELIBERATE divergence -- always with a 'why'. Adding a case means dropping a .json in cases/ and an entry here: both test suites pick it up with no other change.

cases.why: The smallest document the schema allows: one step, one stroke, no style.
Every supported command, a closed subpath, comma separators, two subpaths in one d, and exponent notation.
One command letter carrying two coordinate pairs is two line segments.
Coordinate pairs after the first in a moveto are implicit linetos, per the SVG grammar.
iOS Color(hex:) accepts a missing leading #, so the tool must too — the web player adds it back before handing the colour to SVG.
iOS Color(hex:) accepts 8-digit #RRGGBBAA, and so does CSS Color 4.
voiceover is optional; both sides treat absent and null alike.
A string voiceover is accepted and ignored; v1 has no audio.
Only schemaVersion 1 exists; both players must refuse a future format rather than guess.
A required root field is missing.
The canvas defines the coordinate space; half of it is not usable.
A zero-width canvas has no coordinate space to map to the viewBox.
A tutorial with no steps has nothing to teach.
A step with no strokes would pause the player on a blank canvas.
duration is seconds, not a string.
Lowercase commands are relative. Rendering them as absolute would draw the wrong picture, so both parsers refuse.
Arcs are outside the M/L/C/Q/Z subset both renderers implement.

web.messageContains: Only M, L, C, Q and Z

ios.messageContains: Only M, L, C, Q and Z

cases.why: A lineto needs two numbers.
A path that does not start with a moveto has no defined start point.
A lone decimal point is not a number.
An empty d draws nothing; the schema catches it as an empty string, iOS as an empty path.
A coordinate that overflows to infinity draws nothing. JavaScript and Swift both parse 1e400 to infinity rather than failing, so both parsers check explicitly.
A stroke that takes no time never animates.

ios.why: The device clamps rather than refuse to draw: a bad export should not strand a child mid-lesson. The authoring tool rejects, because catching it before shipping is the tool's whole job.

cases.why: A zero-width stroke draws nothing.

ios.why: The device clamps rather than refuse to draw: a bad export should not strand a child mid-lesson. The authoring tool rejects, because catching it before shipping is the tool's whole job.

cases.why: An unknown key is almost always a typo for a real one.

ios.why: Swift's JSONDecoder drops unknown keys. Left as-is deliberately: the device should play a document a newer tool wrote, not refuse it over an extra field.

cases.why: An untitled tutorial cannot be picked out of a library.

ios.why: iOS treats the title as free text and would show an empty label rather than fail to load.

cases.why: CSS colour names are not hex, and iOS parses hex only.

ios.why: iOS warns and falls back to the default. The tool refuses so the author sees the colour they wrote is not the colour the device will draw.

cases.why: Three-digit hex is valid CSS but iOS Color(hex:) requires 6 or 8 digits.

ios.why: The dangerous direction: the browser would happily draw #FFF while the device silently substitutes the default. The tool rejects it so the two never disagree on screen.
